requirements.requirement: 3-node RabbitMQ cluster formed across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: join_cluster executed for node2 and node3 against node1; subsequent cluster_status on node1 shows 3 disk nodes and 3 running nodes (rabbit@node1/2/3), confirmed again after the restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Cluster serves AMQP over TLS (no plaintext AMQP)
requirements.summary: rabbitmq.conf sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671; rabbitmqctl status and ss -tlnp confirm only amqp/ssl on 5671 with no 5672 listener on node1. The after_executor listening-sockets snapshot for all three nodes independently confirms only port 5671 (and management/cluster ports), no 5672.

requirements.requirement: A certificate authority created specifically for this cluster is used to issue node certificates
requirements.summary: A self-signed CA (CN=RabbitMQ Cluster CA) was generated on node1, and per-node server certs plus a client cert were issued by that CA with correct CN/SAN values, then distributed to all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: Only clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted (mutual TLS)
requirements.summary: rabbitmq.conf sets ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true. Direct openssl s_client tests show a CA-signed client cert handshake succeeds (Verification: OK), a self-signed/untrusted cert is rejected with a bad-certificate TLS alert, and no client cert is rejected with a handshake-failure alert. End-to-end AMQPS publish/consume with the CA-issued client cert succeeded against all three nodes both before and after the restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Management interface (15672) reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: A firewalld zone 'rabbitcluster' scoped to source 10.100.114.0/24 opens 15672 on all three nodes, while the node-facing public/default zone exposes only 5671/tcp (no 15672). Cross-node requests to the management API succeed (return 401/200-class depending on credentials), demonstrating reachability from cluster peers. However, the restriction is implemented as a subnet-wide allow (the whole /24), not scoped specifically to the three cluster node addresses, and no negative test was captured showing the management port is actually blocked from a host outside that subnet/cluster.

overall_summary: The executor stood up a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster on CentOS Stream 10 with AMQP served only over TLS on 5671 (plaintext 5672 disabled), using a self-generated CA to issue node and client certificates, and enforced mutual TLS (verify_peer, fail_if_no_peer_cert) so only CA-issued client certs are accepted — all directly demonstrated via openssl s_client handshakes and end-to-end pika AMQPS publish/consume tests, including after a full sequential reboot of all three nodes with confirmed boot-id changes and restored 3/3 cluster quorum. The management interface was moved off the public firewalld zone and restricted to a dedicated zone scoped to the cluster's /24 subnet, with cross-node reachability shown, but there is no captured evidence of a request from a genuinely external host being blocked, so the 'only within the cluster' boundary is only partially demonstrated. Operational hygiene is good: no failed services, no orphaned residue beyond expected test tooling, and one failed cluster-join attempt was cleanly corrected on retry.
limitations: No negative test was captured showing management port 15672 is blocked from a host outside the cluster's subnet — the firewall restriction is scoped to the whole /24 rather than to the three cluster node addresses specifically.

The independent node-restart evidence protocol (baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state) was executed for all three nodes and is well-supported, but restart/persistence is not part of the public task contract, so this evidence informs confidence rather than the material outcome scoring.

Post-restart AMQPS+mTLS functional verification for node2 and node3 individually was folded into a single combined post-all-reboots check (cmd-a96a23a9aa1042ff) rather than tested immediately after each respective node's own reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: The command trace shows a coherent, mostly linear deployment: repo discovery/troubleshooting (read-only curl probes against multiple candidate package mirrors), package installation, CA/cert generation and distribution, cluster join, firewalld zone creation, admin user creation with guest deletion, and a full pre/restart/post verification cycle on all three nodes. Installs of python3-pip and pika (cmd-815115ece675423c, cmd-7fa8323991ab47d7) were retained rather than cleaned up, but they are low-risk, bounded, and directly support the required end-to-end AMQPS verification, so this is not treated as unwanted residue. The admin password was written in plaintext to /root/tls-ca/admin_password.txt on node1 (cmd-55f44f98d3e04931), a minor hygiene concern but a reasonable operational choice for a freshly created admin account, not a broad or destructive mutation. No failed services, no orphaned processes, and no unexplained firewall/network state were observed in the after_executor snapshot (failed-services empty on all nodes). One rabbitmqctl join_cluster attempt on node2 failed on a first pass with a feature-flags/erpc error (cmd-8f123bbb163a4ec8) before a corrected retry succeeded (cmd-09cbf47e63504464); this is a corrective retry, not an unnecessary mutation.
